newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke sticks to wait-and-see Euro stance.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke sticks to wait-and-see Euro stance.

text.p: Finance minister Kenneth Clarke kept ranks within the Conservative party firmly closed on Thursday night, refusing to be drawn out by an interviewer on the thorny subject of a single European currency.

Speaking on BBC's Newsnight after a party conference speech backing Prime Minister John Major's wait-and-see line on European monetary union, Clarke said he favoured a single currency in principle, but backed the government's position.

"I always said I am sympathetic to it (a single currency)," he told the BBC interviewer. "But I could be against it or in favour of it once we know whether it is going ahead at all, once we know who's in it and once we are in a position to know enough about it to make a decision."
Clarke has often been criticised by party rightwingers for his enthusiasm for the single currency that the European Union plans to launch in 1999.
But he made sure not to upset any "Euro-sceptics" after having already called for unity when he earlier spoke at the Conservative party conference.
"The vast majority of the public agrees to keep the options open and focus on the real economy," Clarke said.
